2026.tx: On 22 October 2026, the ISSB launched a consultation on proposed nature-related disclosure guidance. The guidance would take the form of an IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Practice Statement that sets out incremental disclosure requirements, in addition to those in IFRS S1 and IFRS S2, for nature-related risks and opportunities. The consultation closes on 19 February 2027. Why the ISSB is acting now Feedback on the ISSB's 2022 Agenda Consultation showed significant investor interest in improved disclosures about nature-related risks and opportunities. Users were pointing to the absence of a globally recognised framework as a key reason for the low quality, unavailability and incomparability of nature-related information. 688.title: Carbon credits, sustainable farming can boost Indian rice farmers' incomes: Industry experts - India's News.Net
688.rss_desc: Carbon credits, sustainable farming can boost Indian rice farmers' incomes: Industry experts India's News.Net
688.ogt: Carbon credits, sustainable farming can boost Indian rice farmers
688.ogd: Carbon credits, water-saving technologies and sustainable farming practices can create new income opportunities for Indian rice farmers while reducing cultivation costs and environmental impact, industry experts said at the Bharat International Rice Conference (BIRC) 2026 in New Delhi. During a panel discussion on sustainability and carbon credits in the rice supply chain, experts emphasised that investments in climate-friendly farming, advanced agricultural technologies and supportive policy incentives could make sustainable rice cultivation economically viable. Kaushal Bisht, Director at Varaha, a carbon project developer, said the company runs a carbon programme for smallholder farmers covering around one million acres across Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand. He said the company has raised around USD 100 million through equity and project financing, including USD 30 million from French asset manager Mirova to support sustainable farming equipment and practices. The scale has already arrived. It's about more and more folks in the industry aligning with it, Bisht said. He also highlighted plans to establish two gasification units in Sangrur, Punjab, to convert around 60,000 tonnes of paddy straw into biochar, which can improve soil health and generate carbon credits. Barun Kumar, Director of Operations at VKU Certification, highlighted a carbon credit project in Telangana involving approximately 20,000 farmers adopting alternate wetting and drying practices. He said farmers could generate additional income through verified emissions reductions, with approximately three carbon credits potentially generated per hectare in one cultivation season. Without evidence, it's not possible to generate the carbon credit, Kumar said, emphasising the importance of monitoring and verification. Sanjay Sethi, Executive Director and CEO of the Indian Chamber of Food and Agriculture, welcomed growing investment in carbon markets but cautioned against inadequate verification and the risk of farmers returning to conventional practices. Carbon credits have really gone up in terms of so much money coming in, he said, while calling for stronger safeguards to maintain market credibility. Dr Swati Nayak, Scientist and India Country Manager at the International Rice Research Institute (IRRI), stressed the importance of redesigning agricultural incentives to encourage water conservation. Those incentives need to be also enabled, she said, explaining that farmers must see clear economic benefits from adopting sustainable technologies. Deepak Pareek, Founder of HNYB Tech-Incubations, called for reforms in water-use incentives and better prices for sustainably produced rice. Start pricing the rice for sustainability, he said, urging businesses to reward farmers for adopting environmentally responsible practices. Dr Saurabh Badoni of IRRI highlighted the need for climate-resilient rice varieties that maintain grain quality and export competitiveness amid rising temperatures. Garima Joshi, Principal Analyst, Agri Sustainability at S&P Global, emphasised technology adoption, farmer awareness and redesigned incentives to address climate risks and market fluctuations. The Bharat International Rice Conference 2026 is being held from October 23 to 25 in New Delhi, bringing together Indian exporters, international buyers and other stakeholders in the global rice trade. (ANI)

1810.ogd: The European Parliament’s environment committee backs 99 million extra free EU carbon allowances for industry from 2026 to 2030.
1810.tx: The European Union is moving toward a major change in how it gives free carbon permits to industry. The European Parliament’s environment committee has backed a plan that could provide around 99 million additional free emissions allowances to certain industrial installations from 2026 to 2030. The proposal aims to help European businesses manage carbon costs and compete with companies in countries with weaker climate rules. But it also raises a key question: how can the EU protect its industries while keeping pressure on them to cut emissions? The committee’s position differs from the plan backed by EU member states, which would provide around 121 million allowances. Neither proposal should be treated as final law. 1992.tx: Last month, the Finnish Licensing and Supervision Authority (LVV) launched an investigation into whether the development of two Google data centres in Muhos and Otanmäki, Finland, breached environmental law. The concerns arose around a week after Google announced it was making a record €13bn investment in Finnish artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure. 1899.tx: Chart: A record two-thirds of car sales in China are now electric vehicles For the first time, new-energy vehicles (NEVs) made up 67% of new car sales in China in September, according to the latest data from the China Passenger Car Association (CPCA). The figures show that NEVs, which include battery electric cars and plug-in hybrids, captured a record share of sales, even though fewer were sold than last year. This is because sales of combustion-engine cars are falling steeply, a trend that the CPCA has attributed to rising petrol prices following the start of the Hormuz crisis. Indeed, sales of fuel-only cars were down 31% year-on-year in the first nine months of 2026, with plug-in hybrid sales down 26% – whereas battery EV sales were only down 4%. 1861.ogd: Seattle startup Strella raised $4.25 million to expand its technology that tracks how fruit is ripening as it moves from growers to grocery stores. The goal is to help businesses spot potential spoilage and waste less food.
1861.tx: Seattle-based ag-tech startup Strella has landed $4.25 million to expand the reach of its technology that monitors produce to prevent spoilage and food waste. The investment extends the company’s Series A round and brings its total funding to $26.25 million. CEO and co-founder Katherine Sizov launched the startup in Philadelphia in 2019 and relocated its headquarters to Seattle four years ago to be closer to Washington’s fruit orchards. Strella uses IoT devices to measure gases including ethylene, a plant hormone released by ripening fruit, and machine vision to monitor the produce. Its software interprets the fruit’s real-time conditions alongside data such as country of origin, packing date and varietal type. 3341.title: OpenAI working on new $30B raise at $1.25T valuation ahead of IPO
3341.rss_desc: Should OpenAI command an over $1 trillion valuation with this round, it would break records as the most highly valued private company ever.
3341.ogt: OpenAI working on new $30B raise at $1.25T valuation ahead of IPO | TechCrunch
3341.ogd: Should OpenAI command an over $1 trillion valuation with this round, it would break records as the most highly valued private company ever.
3341.tx: OpenAI is reportedly close to securing another mega round of private funding, rather than plowing ahead with an IPO. The AI lab is working on raising up to $30 billion at a $1.25 trillion pre-money valuation in a round led by Coatue and investors in UAE, sources told CNBC. This follows a similar report by Bloomberg a month ago which said the AI lab was working on raising $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation. Terms are still being negotiated, both outlets report, so they could ultimately change. CNBC reports that the UAE funding could also be coupled with a deal to secure more computing capacity for OpenAI from the UAE, too. OpenAI declined comment. Should OpenAI command a valuation of more than $1 trillion with this round, it would break records as the most valued private company ever.

1653.tx: Startups are staying private longer, leaving employees, who typically take a portion of their compensation as stock they can’t sell, with little hope of early liquidity. An increasing number of late-stage startups are recognizing this and offering tender offers to employees. These are transactions that allow employees (and, often, early investors) to sell a portion of their shares for a predetermined price to an approved investor. To simplify the tender process, NewView Capital, which specializes in secondary deals along with typical venture investments, recently partnered with Carta. The collaboration combines NewView’s secondhand deal-structuring experience with Carta’s equity platform. 1069.tx: Faculty attrition is not a new problem nor is it unique to India. Universities everywhere struggle to retain teaching staff. Most existing commentary on the subject follows a familiar pattern: it lists reasons for departure, cites low salaries and heavy workloads, and calls for better pay and more respect for academics. These points are valid but they miss what is distinctive about the Indian case, which is vacancy rates rise with seniority. A Parliamentary Standing Committee report on higher education tabled in Parliament in March 2025, recorded faculty vacancy data as of January 31, 2025 across IITs, NITs, IIMs, IISERs, and central universities. 531.tx: Have you ever woken up to an alarm feeling groggy, disoriented, or as though you could use a few more hours of sleep, even after getting enough rest? One possible reason is the sleep stage you were in when the alarm went off. Waking abruptly during deep sleep can make it harder for the brain to transition to full alertness, a phenomenon known as sleep inertia. However, alarms are not inherently harmful, even when they interrupt deep sleep. According to Dr Nikhil Jadhav, Consultant Neurologist at KIMS Hospitals, Thane, the more important factors are how long you sleep, the quality of your rest and whether you maintain a consistent sleep schedule. 1288.ogd: One year after Piyush Pandey’s death, his greatest legacy may not be the advertising he created, but the way he taught an industry to find extraordinary stories in ordinary Indian lives.
1288.tx: A year is a long time in advertising. Campaigns come and go, new technologies promise to change everything, and the industry finds fresh vocabulary to describe what it has always wanted to do: understand people and make them care. Yet, a year after Piyush Pandey died on October 23, 2025, there is something about his way of seeing the world that feels increasingly worth holding on to. Pandey did not merely help Indian advertising find its voice. He helped it find the confidence to speak in its own. For decades, he demonstrated that the most powerful ideas did not necessarily emerge from sophisticated presentations or elaborate theories of consumer behaviour. 1942.ogd: At 15, Sinclair Toffa watched relatives in Togo wait weeks for money from the U.S. and lose up to 20% of it to fees. Years later at Palantir, he saw large companies lose time and money to the same kind of friction. His company, Mural, now moves billions across 128 countries, and he says its next big customers may not be people at all. Find out why Mural raised $15M, bringing total funding to $28M, and what happens when AI agents start making financial decisions.
1942.tx: Businesses that move money across borders now stitch together separate providers for accounts, payments, identity checks and compliance, and every handoff between them leaves a gap in who owns the funds and who can move them. That fragmentation costs more each year as stablecoin payments roughly doubled in 2025 to about $390B and software agents begin to initiate transactions that people once approved by hand. Mural builds the compliant system of record that closes those gaps, putting accounts, payments, identity, permissions and compliance on a single record. 42.tx: People buy term insurance to ensure their families remain financially secure in the event of their untimely death. A term insurance policy is essentially an agreement between the insurer and the policyholder for a fixed period, typically ranging from 10 to 40 years, during which the insurer pays the death benefit to the beneficiaries if the policyholder passes away. This can help ensure that the insured person's family has the financial support to handle outstanding debts and expenses in their absence. Most term insurance plans offer a lump sum payout to the designated nominees when the insured person passes away. 1996.tx: In a move that could help lower fuel costs for Indian airlines, Goa and Tamil Nadu have cut value-added tax (VAT) on Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF). The state Finance Department issued a notification on October 23, 2026, and the revised rate will come into effect from October 24. The change has been made through an amendment to Schedule ‘C’ of the Goa Value Added Tax Act, 2005. 850.tx: Airbus expects the worldwide dedicated freighter fleet to grow from 2,360 aircraft in 2026 to 3,460 by 2045, an increase of approximately 46%, driven by fleet replacement and expanding air cargo demand. Its 2026 Cargo Global Market Forecast, presented at the Cargo Facts Symposium, estimates a requirement for 2,670 freighter deliveries over the period. Replacements will account for 1,580 aircraft, with a further 1,090 supporting growth. Passenger-to-freighter conversions are expected to supply 1,700 aircraft, compared with 970 new-build freighters. By size, demand comprises 1,140 single-aisle aircraft, 860 medium widebodies and 670 large widebodies. North America will lead demand with 925 deliveries, followed by Asia-Pacific with 850. 1279.tx: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has extended the deadline for the full implementation of revised pilot rest rules, known as Flight Duty Time Limitations (FDTL), by five months to March 31, 2027. The relaxations, which were due to expire on October 31, 2026, will now remain in effect until the revised deadline. A government official has indicated that no further exemptions will be granted after March 31, 2027, with airlines directed to prepare their crew rosters and operations for full compliance. 1336.rss_desc: Opinion | Here’s what’s missing from U.S. air traffic control The Washington Post
1336.tx: Air traffic control reform is needed, but it shouldn’t happen through privatization. The Oct. 20 editorial “Privatized air traffic control would mean safer skies” was correct about needed reforms and safety improvements, but it used the word “privatization,” which readers may assume means a for-profit company would run the system. The system the editorial actually describes, and that nearly 100 other countries have implemented, is not privatization. It would reform air traffic control by taking it out of the government budget and turning it into a utility. Nearly all foreign air traffic systems are run by nonprofit government corporations and regulated at arm’s length by the national government. 1174.tx: The Nigerian Air Force’s 401 Flying Training School (401 FTS) has trained up to 900 pilots for the Nigerian Air Force and Nigerian Navy, while contributing to military aviation development across Africa. Established in 1964 as the Light Liaison Transport Squadron, the school serves as the starting point for flying training in the Nigerian Air Force, equipping young aviators with the skills, discipline and professional competence required for military operations. Beyond teaching flying techniques, the institution instils confidence, courage, sound judgement and airmanship, preparing trainees for the demanding responsibilities of military aviation. 423.tx: It's long been known that flight attendants in the US have not been paid for boarding and other duties on the ground, a reality that has always been heavily debated. Flying has become more stressful, flights are busier than ever, and often flights have the minimum crew needed, putting additional stress on the crew. The airlines insist that flight attendants are fully compensated, but still a fair amount of duties are conducted without pay. How did airlines get away with only paying flight attendants once the boarding door closed? How did the situation finally change? Let's find out in more detail. 1582.tx: Meta Platforms today pushed back the effective date of its revised Commercial Terms and Self-Serve Ad Terms from October 30 to November 20, 2026, after publishers and digital advertisers complained to EU and UK antitrust authorities that the new contract would give the company an unlimited right to use their content for its AI services. The three-week delay was disclosed by a Meta spokesperson in an email to Reuters on Friday. Meta has rejected the publishers' reading of the terms.
